findings.text: The tail-call table defines a progression of checks: a simple leaf with a small arithmetic outcome, several chained stages that accumulate increasing offsets, load and store cases that verify stack memory and frame sizing, and error paths for repetition limit, missing target and out-of-range index. Each entry carries a label, an instruction sequence, an expected numeric outcome, a reachability marker, an optional frame size, and option flags selecting whether mutable state is supplied and whether the outcome is read back from that state.

Observed test-case shape comprises a descriptive label, a fixed instruction list, an expected integer outcome, a reachability marker, a stack depth value, and a flags word. The effective instruction length ends at the first zero operation code, with wide loads occupying two slots.

Preparation allocates a program-pointer table with one spare slot beyond the case count, measures each instruction list with awareness of double-slot operations, allocates a filter-type program, propagates the case frame size and reachability marker, copies the instructions, rewrites table-address placeholders and target selectors including distinct encodings for missing and invalid targets, resolves helper invocations to local addresses or fails, promotes each program to runtime form, publishes pointers, and marks the spare slot empty with matching capacity. Any allocation or selection failure releases all constructed programs and reports an error.
Destruction releases each non-null program pointer in the table in order and then releases the table container itself.

Tail-call validation follows allocate, populate and relocate, runtime-select, execute, destroy. Execution iterates cases, cooperatively reschedules, skips excluded indices, requires a present program, records just-in-time status, optionally supplies a mutable state cell, runs a fixed repetition count, optionally reads the outcome from state, compares against the expected value, tallies pass, fail and compiled counts, emits a summary line, and signals failure if any case mismatched.

Module initialization validates an optional suite selector against three known suite labels, defaults to the base suite when selective filters are present without a suite, narrows the range, then runs selected suites in a fixed order and releases tail-call resources after that suite. The exit hook performs no action.

Test selection prefers a single numeric identifier when set, then a name lookup that scans descriptions within the active suite, then a caller-supplied index interval. Out-of-range identifiers, unknown names, inverted intervals and unknown suite labels each produce a diagnostic and an error return.

The spin-family template pairs a lock object with a guarded counter and a guarded pointer. Access to either field occurs only while holding the associated lock across plain, interrupt-masked, bottom-half-masked and flag-saving variants with paired release, with conditional sections guarded by try-acquire success, assertion of holding as sufficient proof, and scoped guards limiting the critical region. Both mutating and read-only operation styles are exercised.

Mutex, sequence-lock, reader-writer semaphore, bit-based, per-CPU local, classic read-copy-update and sleepable read-copy-update exercises all require acquisition before touching guarded fields and paired release after. Patterns include exclusive and shared modes, downgrade from exclusive to shared, interruptible and killable conditional acquisition, atomic-test acquisition, initialization guards before first use, assertion helpers as holding proof, nested and reentrant read-side sections, and scoped conditional guards.

Test containers pair a synchronization object with guarded data: mutex with a counter plus a second lock governing shared read-only versus exclusive writable fields; sequence-lock and semaphore each with a counter; bit-lock with a word and a counter tied to one bit; read-copy-update with a guarded pointer; sleepable variant with its control object and pointer; per-CPU local lock with a counter stored alongside.

Context-wrapper checks require the wrapper to preserve the inner value across a plain expression, a semicolon-separated void statement, and a comma-separated expression, and to accept a void loop body. Annotations mark fields guarded by one or more locks, functions requiring shared read-side holding, and one intentional concurrent increment excluded from analysis.

Relocation mutates instruction immediates in place. Unreachable helper call sites are replaced by a neutral skip operation. Missing and invalid tail targets are encoded as distinct indices at and beyond the table end. The repetition-limit case expects a self-loop count derived from the configured maximum plus one multiplied by the run count.
Generated tail-call programs use the socket-filter program category, and helper resolution covers node identity, several monotonic and coarse time sources, tick counter and a synthetic test helper.
